skill.name: cosmic-database
skill.description: Access COSMIC cancer mutation data for research workflows, including somatic mutations, Cancer Gene Census files, signatures, fusions, and sample metadata.
skill.summary: Download and analyze COSMIC cancer genomics datasets with authenticated file access and reference guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The helper script performs intended COSMIC network downloads and writes downloaded files locally. Most SKILL.md static findings are markdown or documentation false positives, with no prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent found. The main remaining issues are credential handling and output path safety.

remediation.issue: Password handling can expose COSMIC credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the --password CLI option, use secure prompting or a secret manager, and update examples to avoid literal password strings.

remediation.issue: Downloaded files can be written to caller-controlled paths.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize output paths, reject absolute paths and traversal, and require confirmation before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: The streamed download URL is accepted from the service response without host validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate that the returned URL uses HTTPS and an expected COSMIC or Sanger host before downloading.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes executable shell examples for installs and downloads.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands require user confirmation and should run only in trusted environments with appropriate COSMIC licenses.

content.value_statement: Cancer researchers need reliable access to COSMIC mutation files and field guidance. This skill helps locate, download, and analyze authenticated COSMIC datasets.
actual_capabilities: Maps common COSMIC data types to official file paths for GRCh37 and GRCh38.
Downloads authenticated COSMIC files using the included Python helper script.
Explains mutation, sample, copy number, fusion, expression, and signature datasets.
Shows how to load COSMIC TSV, CSV, gzip, and VCF files with common Python tools.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for authentication, licensing, file paths, and large downloads.
limitations: Requires a valid COSMIC account and appropriate licensing for the intended use.
Large downloads need network bandwidth, time, and enough local disk space.
Does not provide clinical recommendations or replace expert variant interpretation.
Version labels in documentation may need verification against current COSMIC releases.

use_cases.title: Prepare Cancer Gene Lists
use_cases.description: Find and download Cancer Gene Census files for gene filtering and panel design.

use_cases.title: Build Mutation Analysis Workflows
use_cases.description: Select COSMIC mutation files, load them into analysis tools, and filter by gene or tumor type.

use_cases.title: Review COSMIC File Options
use_cases.description: Compare available mutation, fusion, expression, copy number, sample, and signature datasets before download.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Right Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the COSMIC dataset for Cancer Gene Census analysis on GRCh38. Explain the expected file and format.

prompt_templates.title: Download a COSMIC File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the COSMIC helper to download the GRCh38 gene census file. Prompt me securely for credentials and save it in my chosen folder.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Mutation Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow to download COSMIC coding mutations and filter records for TP53 in lung cancer samples.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a Reproducible Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reproducible COSMIC download plan with a fixed release, genome assembly, output directory controls, and downstream quality checks.

output_examples.input: I need the Cancer Gene Census for GRCh38.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the gene census file path, confirms COSMIC access requirements, and prepares an authenticated download plan.

output_examples.input: Show me how to analyze TP53 mutation records from COSMIC.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines the mutation file to download, the key columns to inspect, and a filtering workflow by gene and tumor site.

output_examples.input: Which COSMIC files cover fusions and copy number changes?
output_examples.output: The assistant compares structural variant, fusion, and copy number datasets, then explains expected formats and storage needs.

best_practices: Use fixed COSMIC release versions when reproducibility matters.
Prompt for credentials securely instead of storing passwords in examples or scripts.
Confirm license terms before downloading or using COSMIC data commercially.
anti_patterns: Do not paste COSMIC passwords into shared prompts, notebooks, or shell history.
Do not use latest releases for regulated or reproducibility-sensitive analyses.
Do not treat COSMIC annotations as clinical guidance without expert review.

faq.question: Does this skill include COSMIC data files?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and a helper script for authenticated downloads from COSMIC.

faq.question: Do I need a COSMIC account?
faq.answer: Yes. COSMIC downloads require registration, and commercial users may need a license.

faq.question: Can it work with GRCh37 and GRCh38?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper maps common data types for both genome assemblies.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it make clinical treatment decisions?
faq.answer: No. It supports research data access and analysis planning only.

faq.question: How should I handle large COSMIC downloads?
faq.answer: Check disk space, network reliability, and output paths before starting a download.
